2608.06331.title: Tytan: Interactive Neurosymbolic Construction of Analytic Semantic Schemas from Relational Data
2608.06331.paper_summary: From natural-language query interfaces to automated report generation, data analysis tools need a description of the data: the real-world entities it contains, which columns function as measures or identifiers, and how tables connect into units of analysis. Today, this semantic layer is usually written by hand. This is a knowledge-acquisition bottleneck that limits the scalability of analytic systems, keeps non-technical users dependent on experts, and is itself error-prone. We present TYTAN, a system for automatically constructing an analytic semantic schema from a relational database and, when available, a short user-provided description. TYTAN combines symbolic analysis of the database with LLM-based semantic inference for entity proposal, role assignment, and naming. When the evidence leaves a decision ambiguous, TYTAN asks the user a targeted natural-language question. We evaluate TYTAN on eight databases spanning real-world and benchmark domains along the three axes that define a schema's functional utility: (i) coverage, are all important entities and features captured?; (ii) retrieval correctness, do the schema's instructions actually reach the data; and (iii) characterization accuracy, are semantic types correct? Across the seven reference domains, TYTAN reaches every entity, attribute, and aggregable feature of the expert-corrected reference schemas (100% coverage). Additionally, 100% of its retrieval instructions execute correctly (1,678 of 1,678 self-generated claims), and semantic roles agree with the reference on 92-100% of matched attributes. Checking the underlying data showed the small disagreement is in the reference, not in TYTAN. On a held-out blind test (a live, ten-table database with no declared keys), TYTAN recovers the full entity structure with verified keys and satisfies 100% of the satisfiable expectations of five independent blind annotators.
2608.06331.paper_summary_zh: 從自然語言查詢介面到自動報告生成，數據分析工具需要對數據進行描述：它所包含的現實世界實體，哪些列作為度量或標識符，以及表格如何連接成分析單元。今天，這一語義層通常是手動編寫的。這是一個知識獲取瓶頸，限制了分析系統的可擴展性，讓非技術用戶依賴專家，並且本身易出錯。我們提出了TYTAN，一個從關聯數據庫自動構建分析語義架構的系統，並在可用時，使用用戶提供的簡短描述。TYTAN結合了對數據庫的符號分析與基於LLM的語義推理，用於實體提議、角色分配和命名。當證據使決策模糊不清時，TYTAN會向用戶提出針對性的自然語言問題。我們在八個涵蓋現實世界和基準領域的數據庫上評估TYTAN，沿著定義架構功能效用的三個軸心進行評估：（i）覆蓋範圍，所有重要的實體和特徵是否都被捕獲？；（ii）檢索正確性，架構的指令是否實際到達數據；以及（iii）特徵準確性，語義類型是否正確？在七個參考領域中，TYTAN達到了專家修正參考架構的每個實體、屬性和可聚合特徵（100%覆蓋）。此外，100%的檢索指令執行正確（1,678個自生成的主張中的1,678個），語義角色在92-100%的匹配屬性上與參考一致。檢查底層數據顯示，小的分歧在參考中，而不是在TYTAN中。在一個保留的盲測試中（一個實時的十表數據庫，沒有聲明的鍵），TYTAN恢復了完整的實體結構，並驗證了鍵，滿足了五位獨立盲標註者的100%可滿足期望。
